correctness.rationale: At scale n-2, the forbidden differences are exactly the weight n-1 and n vectors, so the complex is the independence complex of Cay(F_2^n,{j,j+e_i}). For even n, {j+e_i} is a basis and maps j to the all-ones vector, giving FQ_{n+1}; for odd n, {j,j+e_1,...,j+e_{n-1}} is a basis and splits the generating set into one K2 direction plus the FQ_n directions. The actual verifier checks rank, generator images, bijectivity, and every adjacency for n=3,...,8, but the displayed basis argument proves all n.

final_claim: For every \(n\ge3\), \(\mathrm{VR}(Q_n;n-2)\) is combinatorially \(\mathrm{Ind}(FQ_{n+1})\) when \(n\) is even and \(\mathrm{Ind}(K_2\square FQ_n)\) when \(n\) is odd.
limitations: This is an exact combinatorial reduction, not a homotopy classification of the resulting independence complexes.
